purpose: Define the Phase-2 MCP orchestration contract for launching local CLI workers LATER: command allowlist, sandbox/logging, token/cost reporting, adapter boundaries, and Codex review handoff. This is a design/contract artifact only; it adds NO launch/process code and keeps every launch action disabled by default.

command_allowlist_policy.rule: Only launchable binaries on this static allowlist ('claude', 'codex') may ever be prepared for launch; the manual DeepSeek adapter is never a local command. The taskctl subcommands are the ONLY parent-repo commands a launched worker is expected to run. Anything not on the list is blocked and audited.

sandbox.env_scrub: Pass only PYTHONPATH, AIWORKHUB_REPO, PATH, and allowlisted AIWORKHUB_* flags; drop all secret-bearing variables. Values are never copied into logs.
sandbox.network_policy: Orchestrator opens no new listeners; a launched worker inherits host network only.
sandbox.filesystem_scope: A launched worker is confined to the AIWORKHUB_REPO working tree; allowed_writes are enforced by taskctl, not by the orchestrator.
sandbox.rollback: Unsetting AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_LAUNCH restores the fully-disabled default.

token_cost_reporting_policy.reported_via: python3 AITools/taskctl.py usage <task_id> --runner <runner> --model <model> --input-tokens N --output-tokens N [--cost-usd X]
token_cost_reporting_policy.budget_enforcement: token_budget_max is a per-task ceiling; a launched worker over budget is reported and blocked from further launches, never silently continued.
token_cost_reporting_policy.note: Token/cost reporting is per task and per adapter so orchestration cost is observable and attributable; secret env values are never recorded.

claude_cli.detect: read-only PATH presence probe (shutil.which style); absence => adapter unavailable, never launched
claude_cli.invocation_template_not_wired: argv-list template ['claude','-p','<prompt>','--cwd','<AIWORKHUB_REPO>'] prepared only; NOT executed by this contract
claude_cli.boundary: A launched Claude CLI instance is a heavy implementation/integration WORKER only: it runs exactly one claimed task inside allowed_writes, runs validation, calls taskctl review, and never finalizes done.

codex_cli.detect: read-only PATH presence probe (shutil.which style); absence => adapter unavailable, never launched
codex_cli.invocation_template_not_wired: argv-list template ['codex','exec','<prompt>','--cwd','<AIWORKHUB_REPO>'] prepared only; NOT executed by this contract
codex_cli.boundary: Codex is the orchestrator/reviewer/finalizer. A launched Codex WORKER instance must NOT self-review or finalize a task it executed; separation-of-duties keeps executor and reviewer distinct.

deepseek_manual.detect: n/a - external hosted model; presence is human-confirmed, never machine-probed
deepseek_manual.invocation_template_not_wired: No local process: orchestrator renders a handoff packet (prompt + task card + cwd + runner/topic) for a human to paste into the Copilot-hosted DeepSeek session
deepseek_manual.boundary: No local process and no API key is held by the orchestrator; the human is the executor and the gate. Returns to Codex review like any worker.

codex_review_handoff.trigger: a launched/executed worker task reaches taskctl review state
codex_review_handoff.separation_of_duties: The adapter that executed a task is never the adapter that reviews or finalizes it; a launched Codex worker cannot review its own executed task.

launch_preconditions.requirement: AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 (default '0'); without it every request terminates blocked_launch_disabled.
AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES=1 (default '0'); write-gate parity is required in addition to the launch flag.
The runner/topic pair is on an explicit static allowlist; any unknown or off-topic pair is blocked and audited.
The launchable binary is on command_allowlist ('claude' or 'codex'); no arbitrary command is ever prepared or run.
taskctl collision-guard passes immediately before launch; any stale or conflicting claim blocks it.
Plan-only (dry-run) is the default action; a real launch needs an explicit opt-in argument beyond the gate flags, never the default code path.
cwd pinned to AIWORKHUB_REPO, scrubbed env, argv-list-only with no shell invocation, and a bounded timeout.
The concurrency cap (default 1) is not exceeded; over-cap requests are blocked to protect the workstation and the shared task queue.
An append-only audit entry is written for the launch decision (planned / blocked / would_run); secret env values are never logged.
The adapter is available: a read-only presence probe for local_cli adapters, human-confirmed presence for the manual_external adapter.

neural_bridge_note: Per AIWorkHub neural-control-first doctrine, the FUTURE selection of adapter/runner/topic (which agent to launch for which task) must be a LEARNED routing decision, not a regex/keyword cue router. This contract adds NO cue router and NO runtime keyword branch: the command allowlist and runner/topic allowlist are static human-configured safety boundaries, and adapter availability is a read-only presence probe. The intelligence layer (learned launch/route/abstain policy) is deferred to trainable targets tracked as MCP_NEURAL_LAUNCH_ROUTING_MIGRATION_V1, so no hidden regex/table cognition becomes launch authority.
no_launch_code_marker: This artifact and its siblings contain NO process-launch code (no child-process spawn, no os-level exec or fork, no shell invocation). Launch/process code arrives only in the gated Phase-2 follow-up tasks, and only behind all launch_preconditions.
